text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High 5xx rate (504/502) observed for ArgusBank (private deployment) through NLB-priv-gw in us-west-2. Threshold breached (>=25% error rate) — paging SRE oncall.
maria: paging aj — hits spiking, customers reporting timeouts from the tenant pool. I can see a bunch of target health changes in the ELB logs.
aj: on it. do we have impact numbers? are requests failing at NLB or backend?
maria: ~45% errors for argus tenant over last 6m, spike at 14:03. Logs show NLB target marked unhealthy around same time.
samir: looking at the node pool that backs the tenant. pulling conntrack stats and nginx error logs.
kelsey: pinging Argus support to let them know we're investigating, will avoid any risky config changes until we confirm.
aj: thx. samir, can you paste the ELB target health output?
samir: running aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:... --targets Id=i-0abcde,Id=i-0fghij - here:
```
{\n  "TargetHealthDescriptions": [\n    {\n      "Target": {"Id": "i-0abcde", "Port": 8443},\n      "TargetHealth": {"State": "unhealthy", "Description": "Connection timed out"}\n    },\n    {\n      "Target": {"Id": "i-0fghij", "Port": 8443},\n      "TargetHealth": {"State": "healthy"}\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```
maria: note: health check is TCP 8443 (NLB). unhealthy target observed only in AZ-a. AZ-b still fine.
aj: okay could be SG or host-level dropping. samir, check iptables/conntrack on i-0abcde. also sysctl nf_conntrack usage.
samir: grabbing conntrack counters now.
samir: `sudo conntrack -S` shows entries jumping, peak ~98% of nf_conntrack_max on i-0abcde.
samir: `sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` -> 65536. `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count` -> 64500. that's close.
aj: that would cause new connections to be dropped, leading to NLB health check timeouts. any recent kernel updates or config pushes?
samir: i see a deploy earlier today that updated iptables rules via our template for tenant isolation (tightened ESTABLISHED tracking for ephemeral ports). timestamp ~09:40.
kelsey: that was the tenant isolation hardening rollout — small traffic test approved. we did not expect conntrack pressure.
aj: hm. two options: increase nf_conntrack_max temporarily, or rollback the iptables change on that host. which is fastest?
maria: we can do sysctl bump across the dedicated pool for Argus, but that requires sudo + change; better immediate is to open ephemeral port range in IPTABLES so established flows are not reclassified? not sure.
samir: quick mitigation: `sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000` on the affected nodes, that should drop counts from 98% to ~32% headroom. running now on i-0abcde.
samir: applied to i-0abcde and i-0fghij in AZ-a. conntrack_count now ~68000.
aj: ok monitor health. maria, can you re-register targets (or force a health check) after sysctl to speed recovery?
maria: running `aws elbv2 register-targets --target-group-arn ... --targets Id=i-0abcde` then `aws elbv2 describe-target-health`
maria: target transitioned to healthy within 25s on i-0abcde. error rate dropping.
incident-bot: ALERT RESOLVED: 5xx rate for ArgusBank reduced below threshold.
kelsey: great. can we make a safer mitigation that doesn't rely on manual sysctl increases? we should avoid hitting conntrack long-term.
aj: yes. root cause seems to be interaction of tightened iptables rules + connection churn pattern for this tenant (lots of short-lived connections). plan: revert the iptables rule in the tenant-hardening rollout for Argus dedicated pool, instrument better, and push a controlled fix.
samir: I also found a crontab on that host that runs a nightly load-test earlier than expected? it was added by infra-qa. contributed to churn. removed it.
maria: summary for incident log: 1) today 13:40 deploy tightened IPTABLES for tenant isolation 2) by 14:03 conntrack exhausted on AZ-a hosts 3) NLB health checks started failing -> NLB marked targets unhealthy -> customer 5xxs 4) mitigation: bumped nf_conntrack_max -> registered targets -> traffic recovered -> removed load-test cron 5) next steps: revert iptables change for Argus pool, add circuit-breaker to prevent churn from killing pool.
aj: agree. Kelsey, can you own customer comms (post-incident note to Argus support) that we mitigated and are doing root cause. keep it simple: we introduced a tightening change that caused resource exhaustion; we restored service and will follow up with permanent fix.
kelsey: on it, drafting message now. cc @security for the IPTABLES policy question.
incident-bot: paging escalation: Please acknowledge postmortem within 24h.
aj: will open incident ticket and assign to eng-runtime (samir + maria) for the rollback and patch. also schedule sticky alert for nf_conntrack usage across dedicated pools.
maria: adding a temporary autoscale alarm: if conntrack > 80% in any host, scale an extra node to the Argus pool.
samir: also adding a dashboard for conntrack pressure and connection churn rate per-tenant.
maria: commands we used (for ticket):
```
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000
cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count
sudo iptables -nvL
curl -I http://127.0.0.1:8443/health || nc -vz 127.0.0.1 8443
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn <arn>
```
aj: nice. for the postmortem we should include timeline, root cause, mitigation, and a prevention checklist: limit iptables tightening to canary hosts, pre-rollout conntrack pressure tests, automatic conntrack bump & alert runbook, and update the isolation policy templates to be conntrack-friendly.
kelsey: draft to Argus ready, will send after you ack. message says we'll schedule a follow-up call tomorrow to review permanent fixes. :+1:
maria: all good. closing the active paging. thanks team. :shipit:
deploy-bot: noted deployment freeze for tenant-hardening rollout until incident ticket cleared.
aj: reopening to-dos: - roll back iptables change for Argus pool (samir) - permanent fix PR with conntrack-safe rules (maria) - dashboard & alarms (samir) - customer comms sent (kelsey)
incident-bot: thread archived after 4h of stable metrics.
